title: Serve a ping-pong ball: toss it up, hit it on the way down, one bounce on each side of the net
instruction: Serve the ping-pong ball so it bounces once on your side and once past the net, then put the paddle down.
context: Kitchen-table ping-pong with a clamp-on net set is a common home game, and every rally starts with a serve: the free hand tosses the ball straight up out of open fingers and the paddle hand strikes it on the way down so it bounces on the server's half, clears the net and lands on the far half. Two hands, distinct roles, timing on a 2.7 g ball in free flight.
setup: Table frame: origin on table top between arm bases (y +-30.5 cm), x fwd, y left, cm. Table top x -19..91, y -65..65. Clamp-on net (Franklin Table Tennis To Go type) across x 36.0, 15.25 cm high, posts outside both edges. Paddle (blade 15.7x15.0x1.0, handle 10x3.2x2.6, 170 g) flat, handle centre (28,-25), blade toward +y, red up. ITTF 40 mm 2.7 g ball in an upturned 38 mm bottle cap (30 mm bore, 12 mm tall, taped) at (24,22).
scoring: 0 if the paddle hits the ball while it touches the tossing hand, if the ball touches the tossing hand again after the toss or anything but the paddle before the strike, or if the paddle hits it twice. 0.25: ball left the fingers, rose >=16 cm above that point, then struck while falling by the blade moving into it at >=0.2 m/s; 0.5: next contact is a bounce on the server's half (x<36); 0.75: the contact after that is a bounce on the far half (x 36..91, net untouched); 1.0: paddle lying flat on the table (within 10 deg), not held, still 2 s, jaws open, grippers >=10 cm from it, arms still 2 s.
reset_notes: Put the ball back in the bottle cap at (24, 22) cm and lay the paddle flat with its handle centre at (28, -25) cm, handle along +y, blade toward +y, red side up. Check the net is clamped at the table's middle (x 36 cm) at 15.25 cm.
fidelity: Rigid parts at true size: ITTF 40 mm 2.7 g ball (restitution 0.89 per ITTF bounce test, 0.4/s damping for air drag, CCD), rigid 15.25 cm net at mid-table, 170 g paddle (rubber restitution taken as the ball's). The toss is plain finger contact, no joint. Paddle grasp: force-limited pad grip, not a weld: engages on two-pad contact with jaws closed, compliant spring-damper capped at 50 N pull, 0.50 N m twist, 1.50 N m tip; above a cap the handle slips. Opening the jaws releases it.
